newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TUTU BRANDS SPRINGBOKS "MEAN-SPIRITED".
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TUTU BRANDS SPRINGBOKS "MEAN-SPIRITED".

text.p: Archbishop Desmond Tutu, winner of a Nobel peace prize for his fight against apartheid, has chided South Africa's Springboks for being "mean-spirited."
The former Archbishop of Cape Town was reported in Friday's Cape Times newspaper as saying he had considered phoning Springbok coach Carel du Plessis to pass on his concerns.
"I'm very distressed at the mean-spiritedness that characterises our rugby, it's mean as opposed to generous, he said.
"That is not right. That is what hurts me."
Tutu said he would still be supporting South Africa in the second test against the British Lions on Saturday.
He added that with President Nelson Mandela he ensured the famous Springbok emblem was retained for rugby -- an emblem many saw as symbolising apartheid at play.
However the omission of World Cup winning centre Hennie le Roux from the injury hit national squad and the continued absence of non-whites in the team has disappointed Tutu.
"I would have liked to have felt that he (Carel du Plessis) really wanted to get Hennie le Roux into the side," said Tutu.
"Yet the impression I gained was that he was not over-enthusiastic. Why when you've got someone so experienced?
"I would have rooted even more loudly if he had said, 'let's take Breyton Paulse and see what he can do'."
Paulse, a coloured winger who has scored 13 tries in eight matches for Western Province, was taken on last year's end of season tour by the Springboks but has not been involved since.
"He's missed an opportunity in not saying, 'let's throw this young boy Paulse into the deep end'.
"He's doing it with other boys, why not this one who has shown a kind of flair and who would also have made people say, 'hey, it's not a lillywhite team'."
Tutu was speaking on the eve of his departure for treatment the the United States in his continuing battle against prostate cancer.
He added he would most like a Springbok win as a leaving present.
The Springboks are 1-0 down in the series.
